newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds higher, may be awaiting 1997 influx.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds higher, may be awaiting 1997 influx.

text.p: Emerging debt prices rose modestly in very light trading on Friday, continuing their recent up-trend, traders said.

Overall, Brady debt was up 1/8 to 3/4 of a point by late afternoon. Gains in U.S. Treasuries helped buoy prices over the past couple of days, as did year-end portfolio maneuvering, traders and analysts said.

"It might be positioning ... in anticipation of new allocations from institutional investors at the beginning of next year," said Kurt Schmid, executive vice president and head of propietary trading at SBC Capital Markets Inc.
However, thin volume probably exaggerated that effect, Schmid said.
"You have to bear in mind (that) right now it's a very thin holiday market, with probably five or 10 percent of normal trading volume," he said.
Among specific issues, Russian and Argentine debt performed particularly well, traders said.

Russia's dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR was quoted up 3/4 at 79-5/8 bid. Some traders said President Boris Yeltsin's return to work cheered investors, but others disagreed, saying Russian debt was simply playing catch-up.
"Russia was lagging a little bit," Schmid said. "It has caught up today."
Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were up 5/8 of a point at 64-1/8 bid by late afternoon, and discounts AR425C23=RR were up 3/4 at 77-1/2 bid, traders said.
Traders said market activity was characterized by a lack of selling rather than an abundance of buying. "People are just happy to be here, riding a little higher," one trader said.
In the broader market, Brazil "C" bonds BRD8D14=RR were up 3/8 of a point at 74-1/4, Venezuelan Pars VZ675C20=RR were up 1/2 at 76-3/4 bid and Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR were up 3/8 at 73-3/4 bid.
Peru Citi PEFLG91=RR bonds remained unchanged at 116 bid amid the continuing hostage crisis, traders said.
In U.S. Treasu.ries, the 30-year bond was up 21/32 at 99-17/32, yielding 6.54 percent.
